# requireValidDomain

<link-summary>Returns the value as a domain name, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireValidDomain() — Returns the value as a domain name, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireValidDomain(
  domain: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a valid domain name."
): string;
```

Labels separated by single dots, with no leading or trailing dot or hyphen and no empty label. It is a syntax check: whether the domain resolves is another question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                  | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `domain`                                                   | `unknown` | The value to validate as a domain name.                       |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a valid domain name."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`string` — the same value, typed as a domain name.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                       |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a domain name. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireValidDomain("example.com"); // => "example.com"
requireValidDomain("sub.example.co.uk"); // => "sub.example.co.uk"
requireValidDomain("-example.com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireValidDomain("example..com"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
